title: Reference Python lesson + graded exercise: "variables & printing" (low-risk exemplar, end-to-end)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Before fan-out authoring of the full Python module can begin, an end-to-end exemplar lesson must exist that proves the schema, runner, and review pipeline work together correctly. This lesson also sets the quality bar all subsequent lessons must match.
objective: Author the first complete Python lesson ('variables & printing') with at least one graded exercise, original prose, authoritative citations, and pass the correctness gate (solutionVerified:true), technical review, and pedagogy review — proving the full authoring pipeline end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: Lesson prose is 100% original; no prose copied or paraphrase-laundered from copyrighted sources.
At least 2 authoritative independent cited sources are included (Python official docs preferred).
Lesson includes at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise.
The exercise has a reference solution that passes its test suite (solutionVerified:true set by CI).
The starter code does NOT already pass the exercise tests.
Lesson and exercise are schema-valid against the lesson and exercise JSON Schemas.
Pedagogy checklist is signed off by a reviewer who is not the author.
Technical correctness is reviewed by a reviewer who is not the author.
Examples are neutral/inclusive; prerequisites are honestly stated; single clear objective.
output: A merged lesson document (and associated exercise file) for 'variables & printing' in Python, schema-valid, correctness-verified, and technically + pedagogically reviewed.
